who: Historian of early modern Britain and Ireland at Notre Dame; PhD Cambridge.

evidence.says: Notre Dame lists Rapple as associate professor of history, with a Cambridge PhD, and lists Martial Power and Elizabethan Political Culture and his article on Sir Ralph Lane.
The public ORCID record names Rory Rapple and lists the same Sir Ralph Lane article, DOI 10.1017/jbr.2023.2.
The authority identifies Rory Rapple as author of Martial power and Elizabethan political culture (2009).

notes: Both candidates match: p-12502 through the article and p-123056 through the book. The Cambridge doctorate also agrees with own_phd; same_as selects the ORCID record.

who: Harry Jindrich Benda, historian of Southeast Asia at Yale from 1959; PhD Cornell.

evidence.says: Yale identifies Harry Jindrich Benda, also Harry J. Benda, as appointed in 1959, promoted to full professor in 1966, and active there through 1971; he received his PhD from Cornell.
The item is Harry J. Benda, also Harry Jindrich Benda, and links LC authority n50007169.

notes: Full name, Southeast Asian field, and Yale appointment cover the student's 1970 dissertation.

who: Historian of France and Portugal at the University of Toronto; PhD University of London 1964.

evidence.says: The authority's citation for Nobles in nineteenth-century France identifies David Higgs with the Department of History, University of Toronto.

Eric Jennings's AHA obituary identifies Higgs as a Toronto history professor for forty years, with a London PhD in 1964, and discusses his Nobles in 19th-Century France; he retired in 2004 and remained academically active.

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the required department and institution, and the obituary confirms the same work and French-history specialization. The dissertation followed his retirement.

who: Kenneth Hughes, recorded supervisor of Aubrey Neal's 1984 history dissertation at Manitoba.

evidence.says: The candidate authority identifies Ken Hughes as author of Chasing shadows and research specialist at the University of Virginia's Miller Center.
The candidate's CV lists a Cornell BS in industrial and labor relations, journalism positions from 1987 onward, and Miller Center research from 2000.
A separate Kenneth James Hughes is identified as a former English professor at St. John's College, University of Manitoba.

notes: The offered candidate is the presidential-recordings researcher, whose education and career differ from the Manitoba supervisor. Kenneth James Hughes is a plausible identification of the supervisor but is not an offered candidate.

who: Medieval cultural and linguistic historian at Université de Montréal; PhD in medieval studies there, 1971.

evidence.says: Montréal identifies Lusignan as an emeritus history professor, appointed in 1972 after his 1971 PhD, and explicitly lists Eduard Frunzeanu's 2007 Speculum maius doctorate among his supervised theses.
The authority identifies Serge Lusignan with the University of Montreal and includes Vincent de Beauvais (1990).

notes: Exact student, dissertation, year, institution, and medieval field agree.

who: Arthur G. Neal, sociology professor at Bowling Green State University, 1960–1993; PhD Ohio State.

evidence.says: The university catalog lists Arthur G. Neal, appointed in 1960, as professor of sociology with an Ohio State PhD.
The university retirees newsletter identifies Arthur Neal as distinguished university professor emeritus of sociology, retired in 1993 after 33 years.

The author entry for Arthur G. Neal identifies him as emeritus distinguished university professor of sociology at Bowling Green and lists Violence in animal and human societies, the work cited in LC n81090411.
The authority is Arthur G. Neal and cites Violence in animal and human societies (1976).

notes: The author and authority are linked by the same work; his Bowling Green appointment extends through the student's dissertation year. He was in sociology, consistent with cross-department supervision.

who: Scholar of South African press history; Houston communication professor and adjunct history professor.

evidence.says: Houston's history PhD list names Les Switzer (School of Communication) as advisor of Ime Ukpanah's Yearning to be Free under 1993.
The publisher identifies Switzer as Houston communication professor and adjunct history professor, author of studies of South Africa's press.
The authority names Les Switzer, also Lester Ernest Switzer, and cites his The Black press in ... (1979).

notes: The university directly confirms the exact student and dissertation; institution and press-history publications agree with the candidate.

who: Joseph Benedict Warren, historian of colonial Mexico and Michoacán, University of Maryland history professor until 1993.

evidence.says: INAH identifies Joseph Benedict Warren as a University of Maryland history professor who retired in 1993 and continued researching Michoacán.
The Jason W. Warren authority cites Connecticut unscathed (2014) and Landpower in the long war (2019), identifying its author with the US Army.
Jason W. Warren describes his field as military history specializing in Connecticut's colonial period.
The John Warren authority identifies the author of The Christian mission to the aborigines of New Zealand (1863).

notes: Neither candidate is Joseph Benedict Warren: p-77301 is Jason W. Warren, the Connecticut military historian; p-143876's supplied authority is the nineteenth-century New Zealand mission author.
